description: The Israeli laissez-passer, a red-covered travel document issued for two years by the Ministry of Interior to people who cannot obtain an Israeli passport - generally Arab residents of East Jerusalem and Druze permanent residents of the Golan. It is not a passport.
energy_note: A travel document, explicitly not a passport.

description: Holders are treated as permanent residents rather than citizens, and their nationality is listed as 'Undefined', 'Foreign', or 'Jordanian'. The document confers no nationality and permits travel only via Israeli airports.
energy_note: Nationality: Undefined. Printed, in your document.

description: Roughly 340,000 East Jerusalem Palestinians hold it - about 75% of all laissez-passer holders. Residents were offered citizenship after the 1967 annexation and most declined for political reasons.
energy_note: Three hundred and forty thousand people, no nationality.

aspect: The re-entry permit is the trap
description: Permanent residents have no automatic right of re-entry. The documents carry time-limited re-entry permits - three years for Jordan travel, one year via the airport - renewable only in person in Jerusalem. Failure to renew means forfeiting the right to return.
time_note: Per renewal, in person, in Jerusalem.
energy_note: Miss the renewal and you have lost your city.

aspect: Two documents, neither of which works alone
description: Most East Jerusalem Palestinians also hold Jordanian passports, but mostly temporary foreigner's passports rather than nationality passports, which cannot be used to transit Ben Gurion. A destination visa can be stamped in the Jordanian document while the Israeli one is used for exit and entry.
energy_note: Two documents, and you need both to make one journey.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the citizenship that exists only on paper
description: One traveller's document listed Jordanian citizenship while the holder had no actual Jordanian passport - and was therefore denied the Jordanian tourist visa needed to transit Amman. The classification is a holdover from the period of Jordanian rule in East Jerusalem.
energy_note: Refused a visa for being a citizen of somewhere you are not.

aspect: And some people cannot get any document from anyone
description: In some cases East Jerusalem applicants can obtain civil documents from neither Israel nor the Palestinian Authority. Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank cannot obtain PA travel documents without an Israeli-issued national number, which requires a record in the Israeli civil registry. Those without one are called Bidoon - without.
energy_note: Called 'without'. That is the word for the category.
notes: Closes the loop with IDR-001: the registry Israel controls is the precondition for any document at all.

aspect: Which is the whole dataset in one field on one form
description: A person exists, lives in a city her family has lived in for generations, and the space on her travel document where a nationality would go says Undefined. Everything else in these seven files is downstream of that.
energy_note: Undefined, and expected to prove otherwise at every window.
